_meta.project: instex Spectrograph Explorer presets -- round 4: VISTA / 4MOST (LRS blue/green/red, HRS blue/green/red)
_meta.companion: data/presets_sources.json, _2.json, _3.json (rounds 1-3); same structure. New key 'recommended_presets' gives the six per-arm presets as numbers; entries may carry 'stage' (design stage of the number) and 'kind' (how the value was read).
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc, and a short quote from the saved document. derived = arithmetic done here from sourced values. alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). Every quote was machine-checked against the saved file's extracted text (whitespace/glyph-normalised).
_meta.quote_normalisation: Quotes copied from pdftotext (layout and raw) / HTML text / reST text; degree glyphs, primes, soft hyphens, dashes and NFKC compatibility characters (e.g. math-italic lambda) normalised; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces; table rows quoted as whitespace-separated cells; pieces that differ only in punctuation/spacing are accepted.
_meta.fits_rule: Source TOAD is a FITS file. Its 'quote' is the verbatim header card(s) of the HDU the numbers come from (checked against the header text). The numbers themselves are binary-table values read with a pure-Python FITS reader and re-checked numerically by the build script (tolerances: 5e-5 A/px, 0.006 nm, 0.6 in R, 0.006 px).
_meta.figure_rule: Values marked 'READ BY EYE' come from the two 4most.eu resolving-power figures (saved PNGs); the quote is the figure caption on the saved HTML page.

4most.title: VISTA / 4MOST (fibre-fed; two identical three-arm VPH low-resolution spectrographs LRS-A/B + one three-arm VPH high-resolution spectrograph HRS)
4most.recommended_preset: Six presets, one per arm; LRS-A and LRS-B are mirror-image copies, so one LRS preset per arm serves both. Common to all six: D = 4.10 m (VISTA M1), F = f/3.0 into the collimator (fibre output f/3; the WFC plate scale 59.4 um/arcsec implies f/2.99 at the fibre input, DERIVED), 85 um core = 1.45" on sky (published; 85/59.4 = 1.43" DERIVED), entered as a slit of (sqrt3/2) x 85 = 73.6 um = 1.24" (DERIVED), 824 spectra per detector (812 science + 12 simultaneous-calibration fibres; 822 if the LRS papers' 10 calibration fibres are used), collimator = Mirror, detector 6144 px along dispersion x 6160 px x 15 um (TOAD 'X = spectral', CCDPXC = 6144). **LRS blue**: W 200 mm, f_col 600 mm (mirror radius 1200 mm; = f/3 x 200 mm), f_cam 345 mm f/1.73, VPH 1351 l/mm, order +1, alpha 18.65 deg, camera angle 36.50 deg (alpha + beta at 463.6 nm, DERIVED), lambda_c 463.6 nm, 370-554 nm. **LRS green**: same optics, VPH 1220 l/mm, alpha 22.68 deg, camera angle 44.86 deg, lambda_c 625.4 nm, 524-721 nm. **LRS red**: same optics, VPH 925 l/mm, alpha 22.65 deg, camera angle 44.82 deg, lambda_c 824.3 nm, 691-950 nm. The LRS gratings and angles are the post-FDR manufacturing specification (L20); the 345 mm camera is the 2016 PDR value (L16) and is confirmed by the 2023 TOAD model dispersion (it reproduces TOAD's centre-pixel A/px to <1% and the TOAD coverage to <1.5 nm in every arm, DERIVED). **HRS blue / green / red** (CONCEPT optics only; the final HRS optics papers are paywalled): W 250 mm (also on the 2019 post-FDR slides), f_col 750 mm (f/3 x 250 mm, DERIVED), f_cam 375 mm f/1.5 (DERIVED: H14 '~f/1.5' x 250 mm; reproduces TOAD's A/px to +3.4 / -6.8 / -1.9%), VPH 3586 / 2836 / 2343 l/mm (concept, H14 = H15), order 1 (assumed), Littrow at lambda_c: alpha 48.11 / 50.73 / 49.22 deg, camera angle 96.2 / 101.5 / 98.4 deg (DERIVED), lambda_c 415.2 / 546.0 / 646.4 nm, ranges 392.6-435.5 / 516-573 / 610-679 nm. Validate LRS against: TOAD centre dispersion 0.308 / 0.330 / 0.434 A/px (ETC doc: 32 px per nm at 450 nm in LRS blue = 0.3125 A/px), TOAD R at the centre 5554 / 7251 / 7766, published R 4000-7700 (<R> = 6500), sampling '~3 pixels' per resolution element (2.92 px median in the PDR analysis; TOAD 2.5-2.7). Validate HRS against: TOAD 0.0720 / 0.0958 / 0.1137 A/px (ETC doc: 89 px per nm at 650 nm in HRS red = 0.112 A/px), published R 18,000-21,000 (<R> = 20,000; TOAD 22,400-22,600 at the centre), sampling >= 2.5 px ('~3 pixels'). The app's ideal-optics R with the 73.6 um slit is 5388 / 6741 / 6734 (LRS) and 22,722 / 24,926 / 23,625 (HRS) at lambda_c (DERIVED, Notes).

Plate scale: 59.4 um/arcsec (UM19, EUSUB) vs ~63 um/arcsec at f/3.32 (H14 concept WFC) vs '~60 mm/arcsec' (WS19; unit typo).

Simultaneous-calibration fibres per spectrograph: 12 (WS19 slide 22; 36 in total per WS19 slide 17 and EUSUB) vs 10 (L16; L20: '1624 for science and 20 for calibration') vs 'six ... attached to either end' (DJ19, UM19; 6 in total or 6 per end).

LRS gratings: 1351/1220/925 l/mm at incidence 18.65/22.68/22.65 deg (L20 manufacturing spec, used here) vs 1351/1220/924 l/mm at Bragg 18.35/22.49/22.46 deg (L16 PDR) vs concept 1674/1298/993 l/mm (H14). The L20 and L16 angles give nearly the same camera angle at the TOAD centre wavelengths (36.50/44.86/44.82 vs 36.50/44.86/44.77 deg, DERIVED).

LRS camera: 345 mm f/1.73 (L16; TOAD-consistent) vs concept '~f/1.7 (fl=340mm)' (H14).
LRS slit: 28 slitlets of 29 fibres (L16, ETC19) vs '30 slitlets make one slit' (ETC19, same table cell).
LRS total coverage: 370-950 nm (L16, L20, L26, UM19, ESOI, DJ19) vs 'from 390 to 950 nm' (EUSUB) vs 372-950 nm measured (D22) vs 367.1-952.4 nm on the detector (TOAD).

LRS R: <R> = 6500 (DJ19) vs 4000-7500 (ESOI text) vs >4000-7800 (ESOI table) vs 4000-7700 (EUCAP) vs requirement 10 x lambda/nm and 5000; TOAD model R spans 4444-9663 and exceeds the published figure (e.g. green centre 7251 vs ~6500 read from the figure at 625 nm).

HRS bands: 392.6-435.5 / 516-573 / 610-679 nm (EUSUB, ESOI, TOAD design interval, DJ19 in A) vs 392.6-435 nm blue (UM19 text) vs 'cover 69nm in the 606-681 nm range' (UM19 requirement) vs 392-437 / 515-572 / 605-675 nm (WS19 summary slide) vs concept 393-436 / 516-572 / 610-676 nm (H15).

HRS camera: '~f/1.5 (fl=340mm)' (H14; internally inconsistent with a 250 mm beam, 340/250 = f/1.36) vs 'F1.8' (H15). The 2023 TOAD dispersion favours ~350-390 mm with the concept gratings; 450 mm cannot cover the published bands (DERIVED, see hrs_camera).
HRS fibre separation: 170 um (H15) vs ~176 um (H14).
Spectral sampling: '~3 pixels' (UM19, DJ19) vs median 2.92 px (L16) vs 2.5-3.5 px (WS19) vs >= 2.5 px/FWHM (EUCAP) vs TOAD medians 2.5-2.6 px.
notes: Status: the LRS installation and technical commissioning at Paranal were completed on 18 Oct 2025 (L26 Abstract: 'This work was completed on October 18. 2025.'); science commissioning and verification follow in 2026 (L26 Sec. 8). The HRS numbers here are pre-construction concept values.

LRS-A and LRS-B are two symmetrical (mirror-image) units with the same optics (L26 Sec. 2: 'The LRS is composed of two symmetrical unit spectrographs including the same optical components'); one LRS preset per arm covers both.

Collimator choice for the app: both spectrographs use a spherical-mirror Schmidt collimator (LRS: off-axis mirror R = 1200 mm with one aspheric corrector plate per arm placed after the dichroics; HRS concept: reversed off-axis Schmidt) -> 'Mirror'.

Grating sign convention for the app: transmission VPH, first order; camera angle = alpha + beta(lambda_c) measured from the collimator axis. LRS: alpha 18.65 / 22.68 / 22.65 deg, beta 17.85 / 22.18 / 22.17 deg. HRS (Littrow assumed): alpha = beta = 48.11 / 50.73 / 49.22 deg.

DERIVED LRS check against TOAD (L20 gratings and angles, f_col 600, f_cam 345, lambda_c = TOAD centre pixel 463.56 / 625.44 / 824.27 nm): A/px 0.3063 / 0.3300 / 0.4353 (TOAD 0.3084 / 0.3300 / 0.4340); coverage 368.3-554.8 / 522.2-723.2 / 688.1-953.2 nm (TOAD 367.1-554.9 / 522.0-722.9 / 688.4-952.4). App-style R with the 73.6 um slit-equivalent width: 5388 / 6741 / 6734 (TOAD 5554 / 7251 / 7766; R with the full 85 um core: 4666 / 5838 / 5832).

DERIVED HRS check (concept gratings, Littrow at lambda_c = 415.21 / 545.99 / 646.38 nm, f_col 750, f_cam 375): A/px 0.0745 / 0.0893 / 0.1115 (TOAD 0.0720 / 0.0958 / 0.1137); coverage 391.0-436.4 / 516.7-571.2 / 610.0-678.0 nm; app-style R 22,722 / 24,926 / 23,625 (full core 19,678 / 21,586 / 20,459; TOAD 22,565 / 22,416 / 22,447; published 18,000-21,000). Because R depends on G, f_col and alpha but not on f_cam, the HRS R prediction rests entirely on the concept gratings and the f/3 x 250 mm collimator.

Fibre spacing on the LRS detector is not uniform: 6.5 px between fibres within a slitlet, 0.73 mm (= 28 px on the detector) extra between the 28 slitlets (DERIVED from L16 Sec. 3.1). An app that spreads 824 spectra evenly over the 153 mm slit gets ~7.1 px per spectrum.

TOAD provenance: the FITS file is the instrument-model input of the public 4MOST ETC (qmostetc 2.6.1). Its primary header carries TOAD = '0.4.1' and DATE = '2023-05-08T09:55:49.775238'; its Dispersion and Resolution HDUs tabulate wavelength, pixel width and FWHM for all 6144 spectral pixels of each arm. Table values quoted here were read with a pure-Python FITS reader and re-checked by the build script; the 'quote' column for TOAD rows holds the verbatim header card of the HDU the numbers come from.
Figure-read R values (EUCAP figures) are approximate (+/-100) and are given only to show the slope of R across each arm; prefer the TOAD tables or the published ranges for numeric validation.
WS19 is a 104 MB slide deck (Zenodo); it is the only post-FDR source for the 250 mm HRS beam and the 12 simultaneous-calibration fibres per spectrograph.
VISTA's native f/3.25 Cassegrain focus (ESOV) belongs to the VIRCAM configuration; 4MOST uses its own WFC/ADC (2.6 deg field), whose 59.4 um/arcsec scale corresponds to f/2.99 (DERIVED).
